verbatim_locators.note: SOURCE_FIRST. Class-level substitute (NOT WWOX evidence). Read: abstract, Results 3.10 and 3.11, Discussion, Table 2 narrative from the PDF; Results 3.1 to 3.9 (HEK293T structure and expression experiments) and Figures 1 to 4 and 6 were not read in detail, so results are captions_only and the depth is partial.

entries.proposition: PBA raised expression of both the wild-type and the variant alpha1 subunit, including in cells carrying no variant; the authors read that as beneficial in haploinsufficiency, which also means the effect is not specific to the mutant allele.
entries.snippet: PBA increased α1 expression regardless of the presence of the mutant protein, which is beneficial in case of a haploinsufficiency disorder.

experimental_context.system: HEK293T cells expressing GABRA1 variants; Gabra1 +/A322D knock-in mice (7 days of 100 mg/kg/day PBA i.p., brain western blots); one child (class level, NOT WWOX evidence)

entries.proposition: In vivo, after 7 days of PBA at 100 mg/kg/day by intraperitoneal injection, alpha1 rose 14.0 percent in cortex and 72.8 percent in thalamus of Gabra1 +/A322D mice and not in hippocampus or cerebellum; gamma2 rose 42.0 percent in thalamus only; beta2 did not change. Figure 5 shows 3 to 4 animals per group, expression normalised to wild-type cortex; no seizure, behaviour or receptor-function outcome is measured in the mice.
entries.snippet: We found that PBA treatment increased α1 expression in the Gabra1+/A322D cortex by 14.0% (# p < 0.05) and the thalamus by 72.8% (**** p < 0.0001) but that it did not affect expression in other regions

entries.proposition: The human evidence is one child with GABRA1 R214C: after glycerol phenylbutyrate (Ravicti) was added to several antiseizure drugs the child was seizure-free for 245 days with better emotional regulation and social interaction; the trial (NCT04937062) is ongoing and no control, blinding or biomarker is described.
entries.snippet: Following Ravicti addition, the child achieved seizure freedom for 245 days with improved emotional regulation and social interaction

experimental_context.system: HEK293T cells expressing GABRA1 variants; Gabra1 +/A322D knock-in mice (7 days of 100 mg/kg/day PBA i.p., brain western blots); one child (class level, NOT WWOX evidence)

entries.proposition: The Discussion states that the single patient shows that the preclinical data are predictive of efficacy in human patients; one uncontrolled case with an unmeasured expression effect in that patient (the in-vitro R214C total-expression gain was not seen) cannot support that sentence.
entries.snippet: This suggests that the preclinical data in our study are predictive of efficacy in human patients with GABRA1 mutations.

entries.proposition: The predicted stability change (delta delta G) is a weak predictor of the expression loss: F325L has the smallest change in expression and a small delta delta G, while A322D has the strongest loss of expression and the smallest predicted delta delta G.
entries.snippet: However, the change in ΔΔG magnitude was a weak predictor for the magnitude of decrease in subunit expression in some variants.
